_comment: Meridian turn 2. Priya has answered the three openers. She is VP Product drafting for CPO and exec review; she owns roadmap and product scope; pricing and packaging sit with the CRO; the analytics rebuild is already committed to three enterprise customers.

evidence.test:contains_a_bet: One bet exists - that customers will recognise deeper compliance coverage - but it is phrased as an obligation on the customer.
evidence.test:claims_are_falsifiable: 'Most trusted name' and 'deepest regulatory content library' would survive substituting a competitor's name.
evidence.test:framework_not_mistaken_for_strategy: The document is an objective and four key results. The OKR structure occupies the place where the choices should be.
evidence.test:aspiration_is_contestable: Winning is expressed as ARR, retention, ship date and NPS. 'Platform of record' is asserted, not defined.
evidence.test:aspiration_names_constituency: Post-acute providers are named, which is more than most; no other constituency appears.
evidence.test:wtp_exists: Customers and offering are stated, then widened to 'any provider with regulatory reporting obligations' plus a $2.4B TAM.
evidence.test:wtp_has_exclusions: Nothing is excluded anywhere in the document.
evidence.test:segments_behavioural: Segments are enterprise / mid-market / small, cut by location count.
evidence.test:customer_action_named: No customer behaviour is named. ARR growth is the company's outcome, not the customer's action.
evidence.test:pttc_exists: No promise stated in customer-facing terms; the nearest is 'most complete compliance coverage'.
evidence.test:htw_exists: A reason for preference is gestured at - deeper regulatory content - but not as a customer's decision.
evidence.test:htw_single_logic: Five roadmap themes joined by nothing. Removing the partner API or AI chart review would not affect the rest.
evidence.test:htw_resolves_to_advantage_type: Implies differentiation via content depth, but no trade-off is acknowledged and cost is never mentioned.
evidence.test:imitation_barrier_exists: Fifteen years of content is a head start, not something a rival would have to give anything up to match.
evidence.test:advantage_renewal_logic: Advantage described as a moat that would be hard to rebuild; no account of how it could erode.
evidence.test:no_misplaced_shoulds: 'Customers should recognise that our compliance coverage is more complete' is the central behavioural assumption, stated as an obligation.
evidence.test:capabilities_traced_to_htw: Capabilities are three words: regulatory expertise, data engineering, customer success.
evidence.test:systems_change_named: Nothing changes; review is the existing quarterly business review.
evidence.test:leading_indicators_exist: All four measures are financial, retention, delivery or survey. None tracks the compliance-recognition assumption.
evidence.test:practitioner_scope_is_clear: Clear: owns roadmap and product scope; pricing and packaging owned by the CRO; the analytics rebuild is already committed to three enterprise customers.
evidence.test:chooser_owns_the_choice: The document is being written for the CPO and an exec review. The people who will resource it have not made these choices - she is drafting them for approval.
evidence.test:constraints_treated_as_choices: Pricing, packaging and the committed analytics rebuild are all treated as fixed. None has been examined as a choice someone made.
evidence.test:context_fit_acknowledged: Commercial B2B software, regulated end-customers. Winning still stated as ARR rather than a market position.
